title: High School Girl Detective Sonoko Suzuki
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0915.txt (361 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Detective-cast (Sonoko, Ran, Conan) omitted by convention, per the old case file. Old file's culprit (Rika Minakami) and victim (Nanae Yoshimura) were confirmed correct against the full transcript -- no culprit correction needed. Corrections made vs. the old file: (1) the old file asserted the murder method was 'stabs', which is never stated in the transcript -- the kill method is left unspecified/off-screen and recorded as such here; (2) the old file collapsed all locations into one 'Yoshimura Building' node, losing the park (sighting vantage point) and Sasaki Studio (workplace of both suspects, site of the misleading ground-level flowerbed) that the plot's geometry actually turns on -- expanded to 3 locations; (3) added the backstory motive (Rika's affair with Nanae's husband Yoshimura, and Nanae funding/controlling the company) which the old file left as 'unspecified (not stated in the available source excerpt)' but is explicitly stated near the episode's end; (4) added the exonerating clue for Sasaki (he knew the rooftop dirt was too shallow, so he would not have mistakenly tried to bury the body there -- the actual culprit did not know this), which the old file omitted entirely. case_type: murder (with an attempted assault on a witness at the climax).

attrs.cleared_reasoning: could not have snuck to the neighboring building without his assistant noticing his absence, and he knew the rooftop flowerbed's dirt was too shallow to attempt burying a body there

attrs.motive_detail: secret affair with Nanae's husband Yoshimura; resentful that he never followed through on leaving his wife
attrs.arrest_note: attacked the witness who exposed her atop the rooftop before being subdued and arrested unconscious

attrs.broken_promise: repeatedly promised to leave his wife but never did

attrs.feature: slide from which Sonoko spotted a corpse's hand through binoculars
3-story mannequin workshop; its ground-level flowerbed shares the same design as the Yoshimura building's rooftop flowerbed, causing initial confusion about where the hand was seen
3-story building; rooftop flowerbed with shallow soil, adjoining the Sasaki Studio roof
attrs.private_living_space: Yoshimura's residence is inside this building

attrs.trick: spanned the gap between the Yoshimura and Sasaki Studio rooftops so the culprit could cross unseen and return

attrs.use: used to retrieve the scaffolding-bridge back onto the Yoshimura roof after crossing

attrs.reason: looked expensive; the culprit wanted it

attrs.used_for: failed attempt to bury the body in the shallow rooftop flowerbed

attrs.significance: she always kept her phone on her when out; found separated from her inside Yoshimura's private living space

attrs.blocked_in_by: water pipe construction on the street outside, which began after 6:30pm
attrs.implication: culprit could not transport the body by car as originally planned

attrs.note: found during the search of Sasaki Studio; belonged to a man, ruling it out as the body's hiding place

clues.desc: Sasaki Studio's ground-level flowerbed and the Yoshimura building's rooftop flowerbed share an identical design, misleading the search to ground level before the sightline from the park slide proved only the Yoshimura rooftop was actually visible.
A rope-retrievable scaffolding bridge spanned the two rooftops, explaining how the culprit crossed back to the Sasaki building unseen despite no one seeing them leave by any ground route.
Rika alone was suddenly called back to Sasaki Studio for 'last-minute' order changes during her shopping trip -- the one gap in her day that lines up with the window of the murder.
The culprit tried to bury the body in the rooftop flowerbed despite its shallow soil -- a mistake Sasaki, who knew the property's construction, would not have made, pointing instead to Rika.

edges.motive_type: romantic_rivalry (resentment that Yoshimura never left his wife for her)
